scope: Bounded external primary-source search for forwarded W. H. de Vriese→J. D. Hooker (21 September 1858) and A. R. Wallace→J. D. Hooker (6 October 1858), referenced by batch-04 witness letters. No acceptance or relationship mutation.

external_sources.correspondence: Willem Hendrik de Vriese to J. D. Hooker, 21 September 1858
external_sources.provider: Darwin Correspondence Project / University of Cambridge
external_sources.outcome: Accessible full French transcription and an English translation, with footnotes and letter details. Identifies source as DAR 180:27, ALS 2pp (French).
external_sources.source_limits: The page states the manuscript is deteriorating and the date portion is missing; the date is taken from an earlier editorial transcription. It is a primary-text transcription, not a facsimile image.
body_evidence: Pour repondre à la question de M. Darwin, sur quelle hauteur végétent les plantes perennantes d’environ la latitude de la Grande Bretagne, je dirai ce que j’en ai vu.
Voila mon cher Hooker la reponse aux questions de M. Darwin.

external_sources.correspondence: Alfred Russel Wallace to J. D. Hooker, 6 October 1858
external_sources.provider: Darwin Correspondence Project / University of Cambridge
external_sources.outcome: Accessible full transcription, footnotes and letter details. Identifies source as Linnean Society of London (Quentin Keynes Collection), ALS 3pp. Footnote 1 states it was sent to Darwin for forwarding to Hooker.
external_sources.source_limits: The actual Wallace-to-Darwin letter mentioned by Darwin is not found; this recovered Wallace-to-Hooker letter is a distinct endpoint and must not be substituted for it.
body_evidence: I beg leave to acknowledge the receipt of your letter of July last, sent me by Mr. Darwin
I also look upon it as a most fortunate circumstance that I had a short time ago commenced a correspondence with Mr. Darwin on the subject of “Varieties”

external_sources.correspondence: Wallace manuscript-database record, extract from Wallace to his mother dated 6 October 1858
external_sources.outcome: Accessible catalogue/transcription record for a contemporary extract in an unknown hand, probably Mary Anne Wallace’s, concerning the same date and surrounding correspondence. It corroborates the date/context but is not the Wallace-to-Hooker letter and is not used as its text.
external_sources.source_limits: Third-party extract with uncertain copyist; no substitution for DCP-LETT-2337.

witness_comparisons.finding: Hooker’s P5 says de Vriese gave no answer to Darwin’s Java-seeding question; the external DCP record confirms the letter exists and actually answers Darwin’s elevation question in French. This supports a forwarded third-party knowledge witness, with French-language attribution and a missing manuscript-date portion.

evidence.quote: Also a no answer at all of de Vrieses to your question about Europæan plants seeding in Java.

witness_comparisons.finding: Darwin’s P11 says the de Vriese letter is not much to the point and that he is glad to have it; footnote 12 identifies it as enclosed with Hooker’s letter. The external full record establishes what de Vriese actually wrote, but does not turn Darwin’s witness into de Vriese voice or a direct Darwin reply.

evidence.quote: De Vrieses letter, certainly is not much to the point, but I am glad to have it.

witness_comparisons.finding: Darwin’s P1 says he encloses letters to Hooker and himself from Wallace and asks Hooker to return his copy. The external DCP record is the extant Wallace-to-Hooker letter, not the missing Wallace-to-Darwin letter.

evidence.quote: I enclose letters to you & me from Wallace.

witness_comparisons.finding: Hooker’s P1 says Wallace’s letter relieved him and that he forwarded it to Lyell. The external DCP text is attributable to Wallace and records his receipt of Hooker’s July letter via Darwin; it remains forwarding/knowledge evidence, not a recovered Darwin prompt.

evidence.quote: I am very greatly relieved & pleased by Wallaces letter which I have forwarded to Lyell
